definition: A filled circle means Tariel is depicted acting, speaking, or being directly observed in that chapter’s narrated scene, including the sustained flashback he narrates in chapters 10–29. His direct first-person narration and his own letters count; the intervening letters within that continuous account also count because he remains its narrator. Being mentioned, remembered, praised, addressed in someone else’s letter, quoted within another character’s recap, or discussed as an absent person does not count. This is an editorial definition of scene participation, not a count of name occurrences, relationship metadata, source citations, or geographic co-presence. Chapter boundaries follow the project’s Georgian text because some English entries are displaced.

excluded_borderline_chapters.reason: The prologue introduces or praises Tariel as the subject of the poem; it does not stage an action or speech by him.
Tinatin recalls the stranger and commissions Avtandil’s search. Tariel remains the subject of their discussion, not a participant in its scene.
Avtandil’s letter establishes Shermadin’s authority during the search; Tariel does not act or speak.
Avtandil reports and summarizes Tariel’s story in Arabia. This strip excludes another character’s recap, even when it paraphrases or quotes him.
Avtandil and the vizier seek leave from Rostevan to help Tariel; the absent friend is the reason for their request.
Avtandil discusses his departure and responsibility toward Tariel with Shermadin; Tariel is absent.
Avtandil’s testament explains his obligations and departure; it is not Tariel’s own letter or a scene containing him.
Avtandil prays before departing. Tariel does not take part in the scene.
Rostevan receives Avtandil’s testament and reacts to his flight. Tariel is not present.

Asmat reports Tariel’s departure and quotes what he said earlier; Avtandil has not yet found him. The Georgian chapter ends with Avtandil still searching. An English entry at its end is displaced from the following scene.
Avtandil travels after parting from Tariel and addresses the celestial bodies. Remembering the absent friend is not an appearance.
Avtandil and Pridon recall Tariel and recount earlier events. Tariel does not enter their present scene; another character’s recap is excluded under this definition.
Avtandil seeks help for Tariel and encounters the merchants and pirates. Being the beneficiary of the quest does not count as presence.
Avtandil explains Tariel’s history to Fatman. That summary is information about an absent character, not his participation.
Fatman’s letter to Nestan mentions Tariel and the search, but Tariel neither writes the letter nor receives it in a depicted scene.
Nestan writes to Fatman and discusses Tariel. Her account of him does not make him present.
Nestan’s letter addresses Tariel, but he is not shown reading it here and has no speaking or acting role. Recipient status alone does not count.
Avtandil writes to Pridon about Nestan and their future reunion with Tariel. Tariel does not yet join this action.
The closing catalogue praises Rustaveli’s treatment of Tariel; this is an epilogue reference, not a narrated appearance.

evidence.reason: Tariel appears beside the stream, ignores the summons, fights the guards, and rides away; Georgian stanzas 84–98 directly stage his actions.

This is more than the brothers’ report: they point to Tariel actually riding in the distance at Georgian stanza 210. Avtandil follows him; stanzas 218–228 depict Tariel traveling, arriving at the cave, speaking to Asmat, and departing again.
Tariel returns to the cave and interacts with Asmat while Avtandil watches. Asmat subsequently introduces the knights, who speak directly with one another.

Tariel sustains the first-person account of his life, love, campaign, killing of the bridegroom, search, and friendship with Pridon. Chapters 12, 14, 16, 20, and 22 contain letters within his own ongoing account, rather than switching to an unrelated narrator. Chapter 21 also depicts his fainting in the present frame.
Avtandil finds and revives Tariel; Tariel recounts the lion and panther encounter; the friends return to the cave and plan the next search.
Avtandil reunites with Tariel, delivers Nestan’s letter and veil token, and joins him and Asmat at the cave. Tariel helps open the treasury and travels to Pridon.
Pridon and Avtandil give proposals at the shared war council, with Tariel present as a participant. Tariel then proposes the adopted plan, attacks, and reunites with Nestan.
Tariel participates in the post-rescue journey and gratitude to Fatman, marries Nestan, returns with the companions, and intervenes with Rostevan before Avtandil’s wedding.

The Georgian text depicts Tariel hearing news of India, returning with his allies, confronting Ramaz, and taking the throne beside Nestan. He advocates mercy, rewards Asmat, and takes leave of his friends.
These unfilled chapters contain other characters’ court, hunting, travel, or Gulansharo scenes without Tariel acting or speaking; they are not uncertain borderline cases.
